questions.stem: Why does magnesium have a higher melting point than sodium?

options.text: Magnesium atoms are larger than sodium atoms
Magnesium has 2 delocalised electrons per atom, creating stronger metallic bonding than sodium's 1
Magnesium is denser, so it needs more heat to melt

questions.explanation: Magnesium atoms each release 2 outer electrons into the sea of delocalised electrons, while sodium atoms release only 1. More delocalised electrons means a stronger electrostatic attraction between the positive ions and the electron sea, resulting in stronger metallic bonding and a higher melting point.
